title: Choose your priorities
summary: Start with 1–3 priorities and choose the single highest-impact action right now.
points: Decide when you will work on each priority and for how long.
Define success, what is practical, and your next checkpoint.
Trust God and take action.
prompt: What is the one action that would make today meaningful?

title: Define the next 5 minutes
summary: Turn priority #1 into a concrete five-minute move. Set the latest time you will take it today.
points: Never leave the site of action without the next five-minute step defined.
Choose baby steps over an oversized lunge toward the finish.
Before finishing, define the next move.
prompt: My next five-minute action is… I will begin by…

title: Bring the energy
summary: Bring energy to the task instead of expecting the task to supply it. Make the work lighter and more enjoyable.
points: Use visual feedback to cut through the story you tell yourself.
Measure reps, not vibes.
Let go of the last action and put yourself fully into the next.
prompt: How can I make this action easier, lighter, or more fun?

title: Act & test in reality
summary: Put the action into the world and let real results guide the next repetition.
points: Launch more. Perfect less. Track what works. Iterate fast.
If it is not landing, slow down until it does, then increase the flow.
Count reps and visible outcomes; notes alone are not the result.
prompt: What did I try, and what actually happened?

title: Extract today’s gold
sub: Notice the return on the day.
summary: Look for the value and learning you can extract from today.
points: What gold can I extract from today?
How can I make today a masterpiece?
What will help me see more improvement tomorrow?
prompt: The most valuable thing I learned or created today was…

title: Review & go again
summary: Review your reps and use what happened to choose tomorrow’s next move.
points: What reps did I complete? What worked?
What will I change tomorrow? What feedback can I use?
What am I paying attention to, and why?
Reset and go again. Momentum is a choice.
prompt: Keep… Change… My next move is…

title: Identity & habits
sub: Set the way you show up.
summary: Arrived. Serve. Give. Creative. Consistent. Minimalist. Focused.
points: Before acting, ask: What is my intent?
Raise the floor with non-negotiable daily reps.
Before finishing, set the next five-minute move.
Make tasks easier, lighter, and more fun.
prompt: What daily rep would express the person I want to be?

title: Decision filters
summary: Check the decision against time, leverage, compounding, judgment, and incentives.
points: Is this worth the time and mental hassle?
Where is the leverage?
Am I optimizing for long-term compounding or short-term gain?
Am I acting from emotion or clear judgment?
What incentives are driving this behavior?
prompt: Which filter changes how I see this decision?

title: Anti-drag toolkit
summary: Reduce friction by removing or automating one source of drag today.
points: What is the easiest way to get this done?
What am I overcomplicating?
Turn boredom into iteration time.
Gamify with rivals, small challenges, or personal records.
prompt: One friction point I can remove today is…

title: Health first
summary: The PDF places sleep, sunlight, hydration, eye breaks, and movement beneath the daily work.
points: Protect your sleep window.
Make room for sunlight and hydration.
The document’s eye-break cue: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds, then move.
prompt: Which basic needs attention before my next work block?

title: Smoking intercept
summary: The PDF includes a reflection sequence for a smoking urge, with a personal timing cue of around five hours in.
points: Why do I want this? What is my intent with this hit?
What can I control right now? Choose a five-minute move.
Visualize the rep streak you are protecting.
prompt: What can I control in the next five minutes?

title: Future Benefit Extraction
summary: Charge actions with future rewards.
points: Connect the action to the future benefit it creates.
prompt: What future reward makes this action worth doing?

title: Energy-Led Action
summary: You supply the energy.
points: Bring energy into the task.
Make enjoyment part of the action.
prompt: What energy will I bring to this rep?

title: Visual Feedback Loop
summary: See truth, not story.
points: Use visible feedback.
Measure reps rather than your mood.
prompt: What visible evidence will show what is working?

title: Consistency > Intensity
summary: Count reps and ticks.
points: Keep doing reps.
Define a non-negotiable daily floor.
prompt: What is the smallest repeatable rep I can sustain?

title: Micro-Move Protocol
summary: Always define the next 5 minutes.
points: Define the next five-minute step before leaving the action.
Set the latest time you will take it today.
prompt: What is my next five-minute move?

title: ROI Mindset
summary: Return on time, effort, attention.
points: Look for the highest return on time, effort, and attention.
Use leverage and long-term compounding as filters.
prompt: Is the return worth the effort and mental hassle?

title: Minimalist OS
sub: A few pillars. One world-class skill.
summary: A few pillars. One world-class skill.
points: Build around a few pillars.
Be world-class at one.
prompt: What deserves focus, and what can I simplify?

title: Fun-Max
summary: Engineer enjoyment.
points: Make the work energy-enhancing.
Use small challenges and personal records.
Ask how the next checkpoint can be more fun.
prompt: What would make this rep enjoyable?

title: Pressure Testing
summary: Launch, test, iterate in reality.
points: Launch more and perfect less.
Track what works and iterate fast.
prompt: What can I put into the real world to get feedback?

title: Focus & leverage
summary: Questions collected from the PDF’s success prompts and personal guidelines.
points: Am I working on what actually matters?
What does success look like? What is practical?
What is the metric? What is the needle mover? What is the target ROI?
What is my intention? What do I want to get out of this?
What do I have? What do I want? What am I doing?
What three levers can I move to create my future vision?
What can I do that will promote deep work?
prompt: The question I need most today is…

title: Agency & perspective
sub: Find a different way into the problem.
summary: Use a change of perspective to find practical options.
points: What are they seeing that I’m not?
What CAN we do?
What would I do if I had 10× more agency? What if I had 10× less time?
What would the best person in my industry do?
What are my problems? How can I find solutions?
What would this look like if it were easy?
What small win can I rack up today to keep momentum?
prompt: If I had more agency, the next move I would choose is…

title: Joy & connection
summary: The source pairs productive action with love, enjoyment, kindness, and social growth.
points: What might tickle me so much today that I feel nostalgia when looking back?
What might love require from me today?
What feels unbearable? How can I make it 5% better?
I feel good — how much better can I feel?
Am I investing in my social skills?
Be kind, bring joy, repeat.
prompt: One way I can bring joy or care into today is…

title: Reps & skill building
sub: Know the game you are practicing.
summary: The document uses cards, games, and experience points as metaphors for deliberate practice.
points: What cards am I playing? What skill am I training? What XP am I gaining?
How much focus will I give these reps, and when should I return to them?
Is the juice worth the effort?
When should I pause, analyze, and adjust toward higher-leverage practice?
Try saying “What do I think about this?” out loud to begin forming a view.
prompt: The skill I am practicing with this action is…

title: Archive & personal examples
summary: These are personal examples and archived cues in the source, not new assignments or current facts.
points: Job-search example: success is a job that fits; a practical route is working where a friend does.
Focus setup examples: “Land work” and an “HEB” checkpoint.
Habit check-in topics: posture, comedy, and podcasting / communication.
Think through the next checkpoint; ask how to make it more fun.
Clarify intent before itinerary; choose flexibility and editing mode consciously.
Content sorting: worth posting? If not, worth saving? If saving, where, when will it be used, and how will it be found?
Archived cues include sustained content creation, focused practice, social energy, and “DBU” (down, back, up).
prompt: Which old cue is still useful, and which can I leave behind?
